base.prompt: Return each customer that has at least one completed order with their total completed revenue (treat NULL amounts as 0). Columns: name, revenue. Order by revenue descending, then name.
base.schema:
customers(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, region TEXT)
orders(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, amount REAL, status TEXT, ordered_at TEXT)
employees(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary REAL, manager_id INTEGER)
events(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, day INTEGER)

tests.expected_query: SELECT c.name, SUM(COALESCE(o.amount, 0)) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY revenue DESC, c.name

base.prompt: For each customer that has orders, return the most recent order (latest ordered_at; ties go to the higher id). Columns: name, order_id, amount. Order by name.
base.schema:
customers(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, region TEXT)
orders(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, amount REAL, status TEXT, ordered_at TEXT)
employees(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary REAL, manager_id INTEGER)
events(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER, kind TEXT, day INTEGER)

datasets.name: v1

tests.expected_query: SELECT name, order_id, amount FROM (SELECT c.name AS name, o.id AS order_id, o.amount AS amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.id ORDER BY o.ordered_at DESC, o.id DESC) AS rn FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id) WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY name

SELECT name, order_id, amount FROM (SELECT c.name AS name, o.id AS order_id, o.amount AS amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.id ORDER BY o.ordered_at DESC, o.id DESC) AS rn FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id) WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY name

base.prompt: Return employees who earn more than the average salary of their own department (ignore employees without a salary). Columns: name, dept, salary. Order by dept, then name.
base.schema:
customers(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, region TEXT)
orders(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, amount REAL, status TEXT, ordered_at TEXT)
employees(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, dept TEXT, salary REAL, manager_id INTEGER)
